description:
## Contract risk

calendars-client `CalendarEventGetParams` at
crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/mod.rs:101 carries
`#[non_exhaustive]`.

Canonical mail-client `EmailGetParams` at
crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:40 does NOT carry
`#[non_exhaustive]`.

Both have public fields. Both have `#[derive(Default)]`.

## Why this matters for a caller

`#[non_exhaustive]` on a struct with public fields forbids construction via
struct literal from outside the crate. A caller writing:

```rust
let params = CalendarEventGetParams {
    expand_recurrences: Some(true),
    reduced_participants: Some(false),
    fetch_calendars: None,
};
```

gets a compile error (E0639). They must instead write:

```rust
let mut params = CalendarEventGetParams::default();
params.expand_recurrences = Some(true);
params.reduced_participants = Some(false);
```

This is materially worse ergonomics, especially when the caller wants the
ergonomics-friendly `..Default::default()` shorthand that the canonical
`EmailGetParams` supports:

```rust
let params = EmailGetParams {
    fetch_text_body_values: Some(true),
    ..Default::default()
};
```

The defensive code is forced on every caller of every `*Params`-style entry
point in calendars-client.

## What goes wrong if this stays

Once shipped, removing `#[non_exhaustive]` is technically not a breaking
change (it loosens callers' construction freedom), but the asymmetry with the
canonical mail-client surfaces in every example, every docstring, every
test using the type. Callers who context-switch between mail and calendars
clients in the same code keep tripping over the difference.

Plus the canonical-template propagation rule applies — either change the
canonical to match (and sweep all siblings), or change calendars to match.
The current state is a regression of cookie-cutter intent.

## Fix shape

Remove `#[non_exhaustive]` from `CalendarEventGetParams`. The forward-compat
mechanism for public input/param structs in this workspace is the `extra:
serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>` flatten field (canonical pattern,
see also crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:62-63), not
`#[non_exhaustive]`.

Note this fix is related to but independent from the missing `extra` field
(filed separately) and the missing `Serialize` derive (filed separately).

## Source citations

- crate-jmap-calendars-client/src/methods/mod.rs:101-114
- crate-jmap-mail-client/src/methods/mod.rs:40-64
title: CalendarEventGetParams is #[non_exhaustive] but canonical EmailGetParams is not — blocks struct-literal construction
